$says: One running order per card in the homepage's table strip. Frame nought of each is what the server already sent, so the first turn is a change rather than a correction. The decks share no country, which is what makes a duplicate impossible rather than unlikely.

decks.name: Algeria
decks.text: Chorba, m'hadjeb, and the Friday couscous that stops the whole country.
decks.title: Couscous on Friday

decks.name: Cameroon
decks.text: Bitterleaf and groundnut ndolé, plantain, and whole fish grilled on the sand at Kribi within sight of the boat.
decks.title: Ndole, Poulet DG and Grilled Fish

decks.name: South Africa
decks.text: Fire is a national institution; Durban curry and Cape Malay bobotie came from two very different arrivals.
decks.title: Braai, Bunny Chow, Curry

decks.name: Mali
decks.text: Groundnut stew, and Nile perch grilled whole on the riverbank at Mopti.
decks.title: Tigadege Na and Capitaine

decks.name: Chad
decks.text: Millet boule with sauce, and Nile perch off the Chari grilled on the bank.
decks.title: Boule and Grilled Capitaine

decks.name: Eritrea
decks.text: Eritrean stews on injera, and an Italian coffee culture that never left.
decks.title: Injera, Zigni and Macchiato

decks.name: Lesotho
decks.text: Maize papa with wild greens, and motoho — fermented sorghum drink.
decks.title: Papa, Moroho and Motoho

decks.name: Namibia
decks.text: Game meat over coals, biltong on every counter, and German bread that is actually German.
decks.title: Braai and Biltong

decks.name: Somalia
decks.text: Camel milk, bariis iskukaris spiced with cumin and cardamom, and Somali tea with ginger.
decks.title: Camel Milk and Bariis

decks.name: Angola
decks.text: Funge with muamba de galinha, calulu with dried fish, and Portuguese pastries after.
decks.title: Funge, Muamba and Calulu

decks.name: Nigeria
decks.text: Suya off the grill at night, egusi with pounded yam, and the jollof question again.
decks.title: Jollof, Suya and Egusi

decks.name: Kenya
decks.text: Goat roasted over charcoal, maize meal, sukuma wiki, and coastal biryani that came in by dhow.
decks.title: Nyama Choma and Ugali

decks.name: Uganda
decks.text: Steamed green banana with groundnut sauce, chicken cooked in banana leaf, and an egg rolled in a chapati on every corner.
decks.title: Rolex, Matoke, Luwombo

decks.name: Comoros
decks.text: Lobster off the reef, pilao rice with cardamom, and vanilla and clove in everything.
decks.title: Langouste and Pilao

decks.name: Eswatini
decks.text: Pumpkin with maize, emasi soured milk, and braai everywhere.
decks.title: Sidvudvu and Emasi

decks.name: Liberia
decks.text: Palm butter soup, cassava fufu, and a jollof Liberians will argue about at length.
decks.title: Jollof, Palm Butter and Fufu

decks.name: Niger
decks.text: Millet paste with sauce, and kilishi — beef dried thin and spiced, the best in the region.
decks.title: Millet, Djerma Rice and Kilishi

decks.name: South Sudan
decks.text: Sorghum asida, kisra flatbread, and Nile perch grilled on the bank.
decks.title: Kisra, Asida and Fish

decks.name: Benin
decks.text: Amiwo — maize with tomato and chicken — and fish straight off the Grand-Popo beach.
decks.title: Amiwo and Grilled Fish

decks.name: Ghana
decks.text: The jollof argument is unwinnable; the tilapia off the grill with banku settles it.
decks.title: Jollof, Banku and Grilled Tilapia

decks.name: Tanzania
decks.text: Cloves and cardamom from the Zanzibar plantations, grilled seafood at Forodhani, and ugali everywhere else.
decks.title: Spice, Ugali, Urojo

decks.name: Mozambique
decks.text: Prawns with peri-peri, and matapa — cassava leaf and coconut — with rice.
decks.title: Peri-Peri and Matapa

decks.name: Congo
decks.text: Cassava leaf, and chicken in palm nut sauce — the dish of both Congos.
decks.title: Saka-Saka and Poulet Moambe

decks.name: Gabon
decks.text: Chicken in palm nut nyembwe sauce, and river fish smoked over a slow fire.
decks.title: Nyembwe and Smoked Fish

decks.name: Libya
decks.text: Bazin with lamb and paprika, couscous on Fridays, and shorba on the table all Ramadan.
decks.title: Bazin and Bsisa

decks.name: Rwanda
decks.text: Grilled goat brochettes, cassava leaf isombe, tilapia from Kivu, and some of the best coffee grown anywhere.
decks.title: Brochettes and Isombe

decks.name: Sudan
decks.text: Ful medames for breakfast everywhere, kisra sorghum flatbread, and coffee spiced with ginger.
decks.title: Ful and Kisra

decks.name: Botswana
decks.text: Slow-pounded beef and sorghum porridge, and braai wherever there is a fire.
decks.title: Seswaa and Bogobe

decks.name: Senegal
decks.text: Rice and fish, cooked in one pot, and the national dish by common consent.
decks.title: Thieboudienne

decks.name: Egypt
decks.text: Breakfast is ful and bread; lunch is koshary; both are older than most cuisines.
decks.title: Ful, Koshary and Bread

decks.name: Madagascar
decks.text: Rice three times a day, and romazava — beef and greens — with it.
decks.title: Romazava and Rice

decks.name: Djibouti
decks.text: Spiced rice with lamb, and whole fish baked in a Yemeni clay oven on the coast.
decks.title: Skoudehkaris and Yemeni Fish

decks.name: The Gambia
decks.text: Benachin — one-pot rice — and domoda, groundnut stew with lamb.
decks.title: Benachin and Domoda

decks.name: Malawi
decks.text: Nsima with relish, and chambo — a lake cichlid — grilled whole on the shore.
decks.title: Nsima and Chambo

decks.name: Sao Tome and Principe
decks.text: Calulu — fish stewed with okra and palm oil — and chocolate made where the beans grow.
decks.title: Calulu and Chocolate

decks.name: Togo
decks.text: Fufu with groundnut sauce, and gboma dessi — spinach stew with fish.
decks.title: Fufu and Gboma Dessi

decks.name: Burkina Faso
decks.text: To — millet paste with sauce — and riz gras cooked in tomato and oil.
decks.title: To and Riz Gras

decks.name: Ethiopia
decks.text: Sourdough injera under everything, and fasting food that has made vegans of visitors.
decks.title: Injera and Doro Wat

decks.name: Côte d'Ivoire
decks.text: Attiéké with grilled fish, and kedjenou slow-cooked in a sealed pot.
decks.title: Attiéké and Kedjenou

decks.name: Cabo Verde
decks.text: Cachupa — the slow-cooked maize and bean stew — and grogue distilled from cane.
decks.title: Cachupa and Grogue

decks.name: DR Congo
decks.text: Cassava fufu, pondu cassava leaf, and fish steamed in leaves over a fire.
decks.title: Fufu, Pondu and Liboke

decks.name: Guinea-Bissau
decks.text: Rice from the paddies, cashew as the whole export economy, and Portuguese coffee.
decks.title: Rice, Cashew and Bica

decks.name: Mauritania
decks.text: Fish and rice from the river south, and the three-glass tea ceremony everywhere.
decks.title: Thieboudienne and Three Teas

decks.name: Seychelles
decks.text: Grilled fish, coconut curry, breadfruit, and a chilli sauce that is not a suggestion.
decks.title: Fish, Coconut and Chilli

decks.name: Zambia
decks.text: Maize nshima with relish, dried kapenta from the lakes, and fresh bream out of the Zambezi.
decks.title: Nshima and Kapenta

decks.name: Burundi
decks.text: Beans and plantain, ugali, and mukeke — a Tanganyika fish grilled on the beach.
decks.title: Beans, Ugali and Mukeke

decks.name: Morocco
decks.text: Slow-cooked tagine, bread baked in the neighbourhood oven, and tea poured from height.
decks.title: Tagine, Bread and Mint

decks.name: Tunisia
decks.text: Friday couscous, brik straight out of the pan, and harissa on everything.
decks.title: Couscous, Brik and Harissa

decks.name: Central African Republic
decks.text: Cassava as the staple, smoked fish from the river, and palm wine tapped in the forest.
decks.title: Cassava, Bushmeat and Palm Wine

decks.name: Equatorial Guinea
decks.text: Pepper soup with fish, and malamba — palm wine sweetened with cane.
decks.title: Pepe Soup and Malamba

decks.name: Guinea
decks.text: Rice with palm oil and fish, and the sour milk and maize of the Fouta.
decks.title: Riz Gras and Fouti

decks.name: Mauritius
decks.text: Dholl puri off a street cart, rougaille at home, and a fish vindaye that is entirely local.
decks.title: Dholl Puri and Rougaille

decks.name: Sierra Leone
decks.text: Cassava leaf with palm oil, groundnut stew, and fish straight off the beach.
decks.title: Cassava Leaf and Country Rice

decks.name: Zimbabwe
decks.text: Sadza with relish, and meat over coals wherever there is a fire and company.
decks.title: Sadza and Braai
